changements: The Production tab opens on what production will get: the stories the pending work refers to, by epic, and every release-notes entry production does not have yet, with a count of stories, versions and changes.
Choose a project's reference branch from a menu in the header, with a search over all its branches; like a checkout, it stays chosen on every tab until you go back to production.
Production compares the chosen branch with production; Activity, Delivery, Releases, Roadmap and the documentation read that branch.
The project, its branch and who you are now share one compact line under the bar.
A thin bar runs at the top of the page while the next one loads.
La Fabrique extraordinaire can be added as a project of its own: its documentation, stories, delivery, activity and releases show like any other project's.
The version endpoint gives the version number as well as the deployed commit.
A Roadmap tab: a month calendar of versions released, stories closed and epics done, and each epic's progress day by day.
A Releases tab: every version's notes by day, with the stories closed since the previous version.
A Delivery tab: each workflow's runs over 30 days, share passed, median duration, current streak and last failure.

titre: Read a project on another branch
changements: A branch selector on a project's page: read its documentation and its .fabrique.json on integration or a working branch, production staying the reference.
An Activity tab: commits and lines changed per day over 30 or 90 days, and commits per author.
Product Engineers, tech leads and super admins write a request from the project's own form; it becomes an issue under their name.
Drafts stay on the device until the request is sent; My requests shows where each one stands.
A Production tab: the work on integration missing from production, grouped by merged branch, with versions, workflows and a clear ready or not ready.
A Stories tab: issues grouped by epic, with their state, labels, pull requests and branches, and filters.
A project's documentation reads in La Fabrique, from its production branch, with links between pages kept inside.
The app is now called La Fabrique extraordinaire.
Super admins add a project from the repositories where the GitHub App is installed; its .fabrique.json is checked, with readable errors.
Sign in with GitHub; only people given a role get in, and super admins manage roles on the People page.
La Fabrique is online, with its home page.
